entities.summary:
Chen Zhuo (b. 235 CE) was a renowned astronomer and urban planner of the Classical era, active in the Global region. His most notable work, the 'Cosmic City Plan,' was a comprehensive design for a new capital city that incorporated innovative astronomical observations and urban planning principles. The plan was heavily influenced by his mentor, the famous astronomer Zhang Heng, and showcased Chen's expertise in both fields. Although the exact details of the plan's implementation are unknown, its impact on the development of urban planning and astronomy in the Classical era is undeniable.

As a key figure in the astronomical community, Chen Zhuo played a crucial role in the transmission of knowledge from the ancient Silk Road to the emerging civilizations of the region. His work on the 'Cosmic City Plan' was likely influenced by the cultural exchange and trade that occurred along the Silk Road, which connected the East and West.

The legacy of Chen Zhuo's work can be seen in the continued development of urban planning and astronomy in the Classical era. His contributions to the field of astronomy, particularly in the areas of celestial navigation and the study of comets, paved the way for future generations of astronomers. Despite the passage of time, Chen Zhuo's work remains an important reminder of the significance of interdisciplinary approaches to understanding the natural world.

Chen Zhuo's impact on the development of urban planning is still felt today, with many modern cities drawing inspiration from his innovative designs. His work on the 'Cosmic City Plan' not only showcased his expertise in astronomy and urban planning but also highlighted the importance of considering the celestial bodies in the design of cities.
